The texture of a printed page of text, recovered by inverse rendering from out-of-focus photographs: the first three lines of the page's text, once from each source. From the top: the printed design, the ground truth; a training photograph (number 39 of the 63 the texture is optimised on), rotated in the image plane so that its lines are level, not rectified; the texture optimised with a pinhole camera, which has no defocus; and the texture optimised with our aperture and focus surface. A texel is 0.254\,mm of the page.
